key_insight: Stochastic mid-circuit measurements and conditional resets can drive a noisy quantum processor into non-equilibrium steady states that quantitatively match theory and experiment.
engineering_relevance: The work validates a hardware-ready protocol for preparing collective stationary states on superconducting quantum devices and informs future mid-circuit-measurement-based quantum algorithms.
method: Built a noisy discrete-time model combining unitary gates, projective measurements, and conditional resets.
Implemented the protocol on a superconducting quantum processor for up to 7 qubits.
Studied the interacting Floquet transverse-field Ising model as the benchmark system.
evidence_signal: The stationary state from the noisy conditional-reset theory agreed quantitatively with experimental results and reproduced crossover behavior linked to the model’s equilibrium phase transition.
watch_item: Performance is likely sensitive to measurement/reset noise and scale-up beyond 7 qubits, so hardware fidelity remains a key constraint.
paper_title: Nonequilibrium steady states induced by stochastic mid-circuit measurements and resets on a quantum computer
